relevance_note: Single case report of a woman with a clinical diagnosis of Alexander disease ("We report the case of Louise Davies, a woman with Alexander's Disease."); no GFAP testing is reported for her; five previously published patients are mentioned with individual-level facts.
method_note: Written by hand from a full read of the paper; a small script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Louise is labelled by the name the paper uses most often ('Louise'). Her diagnosis is clinical ('probable Alexander's Leukodystrophy'); the paper reports no GFAP testing for her, so she has no variant row. Five previously published patients mentioned in the Introduction/Discussion are included under the v4 passing-mention rule because each has an individual-level fact (sex, age or a feature): Alexander 1949, Wakabayashi et al 2005, Iwasaki et al (2015), Restrepo et al (2011), Namekawa et al 2012. Some values for these come from the titles in the reference list: the GFAP S393R variant for the Iwasaki patient ('An autopsied case ... with a novel S393R mutation in the GFAP gene'), 'diagnosed by DNA analysis' for the Wakabayashi patient, and 'insidiously progressive cervicomedullary atrophy' for the Namekawa patient; these rely on linking the in-text citation to the single case named in that reference title. The Zang et al (2013) 22 children and other group statements give no individual-level detail and get no rows. Louise's mother and younger sister are neither tested nor affected (the sister 'has always been well') and get no rows. Louise's imaging is CT, not MRI. The 2010 CT text says 'thickening of the frontal bones' while the Discussion says 'frontal lobe thickening was commented on' (bone vs lobe wording differs; recorded as the Brain Imaging section states it). The medulla checklist item for Louise rests on 'marked atrophy of the brain stem structures' (2013 CT) and the Discussion's 'Damage was also seen in the region of the medulla oblongata'. Ventricular dilatation was not recorded as hydrocephalus. The 2000 event is recorded as 'either a stroke or a seizure' and not counted for the seizure checklist item; the 2013 seizure is. Table 1 (WHIM scores) is neuropsychological test data and is not extracted. No onset age is stated for Louise; age at diagnosis is 5 years. Publication year is not printed in the document.
